threats.name: Use After Free
threats.rationale: Use after free needs manual deallocation. Go is garbage collected: a live reference never dangles and there is no free. The residual routes are unsafe, cgo and a data race that tears a slice, string or interface header (the Go memory model gives racy programs no memory-safety guarantee), which is why the registry subset is go_race_free and not gc_runtimes. The library has no unsafe, cgo, reflect or goroutine; its package-level state is seven read-only gate instances (gates.go:70-78).

closed_by.detail: Go checks every slice and array index (an out-of-range index is a runtime panic, never a read or write past the end), is garbage collected (no free, so no double free or use after free), and zero-initialises every variable. Holds only for a package with no unsafe, cgo, reflect-set or linkname, and only for race-free programs: a data race on a slice header, string header or interface value can tear it and break memory safety (the Go memory model says so). A statement about the language, not a check on the package.

threats.name: NULL Pointer Dereference
threats.rationale: In Go a nil dereference is a run-time panic (runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference), not memory corruption, but it is a reachable wrong error. Nil-able surface: DFlipFlop takes a *FlipFlopState and substitutes a fresh state when it is nil (sequential.go:331-340); Counter takes a *CounterState and panics with a plain string when it is nil (:611-613); Register and ShiftRegister take a nil-able slice; TriState returns a nil *int by design for high-Z (combinational.go:595-611), so every caller that dereferences the result without a check panics; the exported Operation type has an unexported map that is nil in a zero value, so `(&Operation[int]{}).AddProperty(...)` writes to a nil map and panics (gen_capabilities.go:76-89). InvalidBitError.Error is nil-safe (gates.go:121-125, tested security_test.go:25-33). The gates themselves take ints and cannot receive nil.

closed_by.detail: Flow analysis that no public function dereferences a pointer, map or interface parameter that may be nil, and that every nil-able result is documented: TriState returns a nil *int by design for high-Z (combinational.go:595-611), DFlipFlop and Counter accept a *State that may be nil (sequential.go:331-340, :611-613; Counter panics with a plain string, DFlipFlop substitutes a fresh state).

threats.name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary
threats.rationale: Registry name: Integer Overflow to Buffer Boundary (wraparound that yields a wrong buffer size or offset); this is not "integer overflow in general" (go.integer-width-and-wraparound). In Go signed overflow wraps by definition and every make() length is checked against a package constant before use: MaxWidth 65536 and MaxSelectBits 16 (gates.go:744-752), MaxCounterWidth 64, and the 1<<n shift only after n <= 16 (combinational.go:346-353). Without those caps a caller-supplied n >= 63 would make 1<<n zero or negative and make() would panic or exhaust memory; the caps were added in PR #19935 (SEC-008 equivalent) and are tested at the boundary (security_test.go:50-89).

closed_by.detail: security_test.go:50-117: Decoder, MuxN, Demux, Encoder, PriorityEncoder and Counter are accepted at their caps (MaxSelectBits 16, MaxWidth 65536, MaxCounterWidth 64) and rejected above them, including math.MaxInt and 1<<62 for Demux; a bad bit in Counter state and in every FlipFlopState field is rejected on every path.

Value-range dataflow (not a text search): every shift count and every make() size is shown to be bounded by a package constant. Sites: 1<<MaxSelectBits (gates.go:750), `1 << n` after the n <= 16 check (combinational.go:346-353), the halving loops `tmp >>= 1` (:192,:276,:447,:519), `(i>>bitPos)&1` (:372,:454,:547), make([]int, nOutputs) after the MaxWidth check (:288,:361,:452,:545) and make([]int, width) after the MaxCounterWidth check (sequential.go:620-644).

threats.name: Code Injection / Eval
threats.rationale: Go has no eval, but a Go package can still load or build code at run time (plugin.Open, cgo, reflect Call, a template engine, os/exec of the go tool). The library uses none (imports fmt and transistors only). VER15a section 1.3 says a compiled lane that wants to exclude the class needs an analyzer rule banning those constructs, and that the rule's definition decides whether it counts as compiled_languages_no_eval; the merged Go analyzer bans plugin.Open, import "C", linkname and reflect Call/CallSlice/MethodByName (banned.go:46-52) but not reflect.MakeFunc, templates, go/parser or os/exec-of-go.

closed_by.detail: Go has no eval, but it can load or build code: plugin.Open, cgo, reflect.MakeFunc and reflect Call, go/types or go/parser feeding an interpreter, text/template or html/template Execute on caller text, os/exec of `go`, and //go:generate. The rule bans every import and construct in that list; it is the analyzer definition (VER15a section 1.3 last paragraph) that decides whether it counts as compiled_languages_no_eval. threats.name: Discarded error from the Operation wrapper (result, _ := ...GetResult())
threats.rationale: Every gate writes `result, _ := StartNew[int](...).PanicOnUnexpected().GetResult()` (gates.go:223 and the other call sites), discarding the error: the Go-characteristic form of CWE-252. It is safe only because every callback returns rf.Generate(true, false, v) (so the error is nil) and PanicOnUnexpected re-panics instead of returning an error (gen_capabilities.go:137-139). Edit one callback to return rf.Fail(...) and the error would be dropped silently, returning the fallback 0 as if it were a bit.

closed_by.detail: Every Operation callback returns rf.Generate(true, false, v) (never Fail, never DidFailUnexpectedly), so the discarded error of `result, _ := StartNew(...).GetResult()` (gates.go:223 and the 40 other call sites) can only be nil. With PanicOnUnexpected set, an unexpected failure re-panics (gen_capabilities.go:137-139) instead of returning an error.
Every gate callback ends with rf.Generate(true, false, ...) and the wrapper is built with PanicOnUnexpected(), so the error that every gate discards (`result, _ :=`) is always nil.
